question: Fill in the blank: The Federal Court of India under the Government of India Act, 1935 was set up in ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1937**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Federal Court of India was established on **1 October 1937**, under the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
• The court had original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction, but its powers were limited compared to the current Supreme Court.
 
• It served as the predecessor to the Supreme Court of India, which was established on 28 January 1950, after India became a republic.
 
• The Federal Court had jurisdiction over disputes between provinces and federal matters, with appeals going directly to the Privy Council in London.
 
• The first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of India was **Sir Maurice Gwyer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1936**:

 
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935, which led to the establishment of the Federal Court, came into effect in 1936.
 
• This act was the longest piece of legislation enacted by the British Parliament and served as the basis for constitutional developments in India.
 
• However, the Federal Court itself was not established until the following year, in 1937.
 
 
 
• **1939**:
 
 
• World War II began in 1939, significantly impacting India and its governance under British rule.
 
• During this period, the Federal Court of India continued to function but did not see any major structural changes.
 
 
 
• **1942**:
 
 
• In 1942, the Quit India Movement was launched, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• The Federal Court played no direct role in political movements but continued its judicial functions amid the political upheaval.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**:
 
 
• This act introduced provincial autonomy and a federal structure in British India.
 
• It laid the foundation for the establishment of the Federal Court of India.
 
• The act also proposed the establishment of a bicameral legislature at the center and expanded the franchise.
